intro.data: You already know one route from the start to the goal: through Clean Table (B), using Parser then Charter. Build a different route — through Sample (D) — that arrives at the same goal.
intro.alchemy: You already know one route from the start to the goal: through Ingot (B), using Smelter then Toolsmith. Build a different route — through Powder (D) — that arrives at the same goal.
intro.spellcraft: You already know one route from the start to the goal: through Flame (B), using Ignition then Kindler. Build a different route — through Mote (D) — that arrives at the same goal.
intro.abstract: You already know one route from A to C: through B, using f then g. Build a different route — through D — that arrives at the same goal.

goal.data: Wire the start through Sampler and Plotter (via Sample) to reach the same goal the other route reaches.
goal.alchemy: Wire the start through Grinder and Caster (via Powder) to reach the same goal the other route reaches.
goal.spellcraft: Wire the start through Siphon and Focuser (via Mote) to reach the same goal the other route reaches.
goal.abstract: Wire the start through h and k (via D) to reach C, the same goal as g ∘ f.

afterSuccess.data: Two different routes, the same start and the same goal. When routes like these agree, we say the diagram commutes.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Two different routes, the same start and the same goal. When routes like these agree, we say the diagram commutes.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Two different workings, the same start and the same goal. When routes like these agree, we say the diagram commutes.
afterSuccess.abstract: Two different paths, the same source and the same target. When paths like these agree, we say the diagram commutes.

reveal.summary: Different routes that share a start and an end can produce the same result. A diagram where parallel routes agree is called a commutative diagram.
reveal.moreFormal: Both g ∘ f and k ∘ h are arrows A → C. Saying the square commutes asserts they are equal as morphisms — the route you take through the diagram does not change the result.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: Two different implementations that pass exactly the same tests.
